title: Layang-Layang Plastik
subject: a father and his eight-year-old daughter Aisyah in the padang behind their Shah Alam flat, launching a kite made from a supermarket plastic bag and satay sticks that keeps nosediving until she ties her old school tie on as the tail
caption: Malay doo-wop revival in 1950s vocal-group style. Upright piano pounding triplet chords, slapped upright bass, brushed drums with a shuffle, honking tenor saxophone solo, four-part backing harmony with bass voice and falsetto. Vintage mono-leaning room sound with light spring reverb. Male tenor lead with a three-man backing group singing doo-wop syllables and answers. 132 BPM, Bb major. Playful, affectionate father-daughter sing-along. No modern synths, no trap drums, no autotune, no rock distortion, no rap.
lyrics:
[Intro - backing harmony and piano triplets]

[Verse 1]
Beg plastik kedai runcit
Dua batang lidi sate
Aisyah pegang benang
Ayah lari, ayah lari

[Chorus]
Layang-layang plastik, wo-oh
Naik sikit, jatuh balik
Kepala dulu cium rumput
Layang-layang plastik

[Verse 2]
Aisyah buka beg sekolah
Tali leher lama dia
Ikat jadi ekor panjang
Cuba sekali lagi, ayah

[Chorus]
Layang-layang plastik, wo-oh
Naik tinggi, tak jatuh lagi
Ekor biru menari-nari
Layang-layang plastik

[Bridge - saxophone solo, then stop-time]
Maghrib dah nak masuk
Mak dah panggil dari tingkap

[Outro - backing group fade]
